interactions.label: Which data source is considered India's most reliable for fertility and mortalit

params.question: Which data source is considered India's most reliable for fertility and mortality rates because it reconciles independent surveyor records with those of local registrars?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CRS is the statutory system for registering births and deaths, but rural registration lags and cause of death is often inaccurate since most rural deaths occur at home without medical certification.

Correct. SRS uses independent surveyors alongside registrars in a representative sample of villages and urban areas, then reconciles the two records — this dual-record method makes it India's most reliable source for fertility and mortality rates.
NFHS is a periodic national survey that captures health behaviours and morbidity, not a continuous vital registration system for births and deaths.
IDSP is a disease notification system built for rapid outbreak detection, not a source of routine fertility or mortality statistics.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: CRS is statutory but incomplete in rural areas; SRS fixes this gap through independent verification, making it the more reliable source for vital rates.
Well done — SRS's independent-surveyor-plus-registrar reconciliation is exactly what makes it more accurate than CRS alone.

interactions.label: In District X, cardiovascular disease shows a very high proportional mortality r

params.question: In District X, cardiovascular disease shows a very high proportional mortality rate but a low cause-specific death rate. What is the most likely explanation?

answers.text: The district has an unusually large population at risk of cardiovascular disease

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Population size affects the cause-specific death rate's denominator, not the proportional mortality rate, which uses total deaths as its denominator.

answers.text: Deaths from other causes are relatively few in this district, so cardiovascular disease makes up a large share of a small total of deaths

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Proportional mortality rate replaces the population denominator with total deaths — a high PMR can simply reflect fewer deaths from other causes, not a high absolute burden of that disease.

answers.text: The district's crude death rate must also be high

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Crude death rate depends on total deaths against mid-year population and is heavily influenced by age structure, not by how deaths are distributed across causes.

answers.text: The case fatality rate for cardiovascular disease in this district must be high

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Case fatality rate divides deaths by total cases of that disease — it is a measure of lethality among the affected, unrelated to proportional mortality.

overallFeedback.feedback: Revisit the denominators: PMR divides by total deaths, so a high PMR can simply mean few deaths from other causes, not necessarily a high true burden.
Exactly — always check the denominator. PMR (total deaths) and cause-specific death rate (population) can tell very different stories from the same data.

interactions.label: Isolation is applied to exposed but currently well contacts during the incubatio

params.question: Isolation is applied to exposed but currently well contacts during the incubation period, while quarantine is applied to confirmed, infectious cases.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: The statement swaps the two terms. Isolation applies to confirmed infectious cases; quarantine applies to exposed, asymptomatic contacts who might still develop disease.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct, this statement has the definitions reversed. Isolation separates infectious, usually symptomatic cases from susceptible people; quarantine separates exposed but still-well contacts during the incubation period.

interactions.label: A case-control study of a gastroenteritis outbreak finds an odds ratio of 8 link

params.question: A case-control study of a gastroenteritis outbreak finds an odds ratio of 8 linking a food item to illness. Investigators later discover that several ill people ate the food only after their symptoms had already begun. What is the effect of this finding on the causal argument?

answers.text: It strengthens the causal argument, because the odds ratio is already high

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A high odds ratio reflects strength of association, but strength alone does not establish causation if the exposure did not actually precede the outcome.

answers.text: It weakens the causal argument, because temporality — exposure preceding outcome — cannot be established for those cases

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Temporality is the one Bradford Hill criterion causation cannot exist without. If illness began before exposure to the suspected food in several cases, the food cannot be the cause for those cases, undermining the causal claim.

answers.text: It has no effect, since the odds ratio already accounts for timing of exposure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Odds ratio measures strength of association from case-control data; it does not itself verify that exposure preceded outcome — that must be checked separately.

answers.text: It converts the finding into a population attributable risk instead

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Population attributable risk is a separate absolute measure describing population-level impact; it is unrelated to whether temporality has been violated.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall that temporality is the one Bradford Hill criterion that is absolutely required: without exposure preceding outcome, even a high odds ratio cannot support causation.
Right — no matter how strong an association looks, if exposure didn't precede the outcome, causation cannot be claimed.

interactions.label: An epidemic curve for a gastroenteritis outbreak shows a single sharp, bell-shap

params.question: An epidemic curve for a gastroenteritis outbreak shows a single sharp, bell-shaped peak followed by a rapid decline, with no secondary peaks. What does this shape most likely suggest?

answers.text: Person-to-person spread occurring over several successive incubation periods

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Person-to-person spread typically produces a propagated curve with a slower climb and repeated peaks as transmission passes through successive generations of cases, not a single sharp peak.

answers.text: A common source exposure where most people were exposed at roughly the same time

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A sharp, bell-shaped peak with rapid decline and no secondary waves is the classic signature of a point-source outbreak — everyone exposed to one common source at nearly the same time.

answers.text: A vector-borne disease following a seasonal pattern

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Seasonal vector-borne patterns are usually inferred from surveillance trends across months or years, not from the shape of a single outbreak's epidemic curve.

answers.text: An outbreak that has not yet been fully investigated

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The shape of an epidemic curve reflects the pattern of spread, not the completeness of the investigation itself.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall the two classic curve shapes: a sharp single peak signals a point-source exposure, while a slower climb with repeated peaks signals person-to-person (propagated) spread.
Exactly — a single sharp peak points to a common-source (point-source) exposure, which should direct the hypothesis toward a shared exposure rather than person-to-person spread.
